The acceptance rests on the evidence this record re-verifies: records and their SHA-256 links, the code chain, the notebook copies, and A4.2-A4.6 recomputed from the artifacts and compared with their records. It also rests on the two run-specific dispositions recorded with it. run_record.json remains the regeneration record (accepted: false). This record and artifact_manifest.json are the acceptance. 7.1.statement: Section 7.1 deviation, run c4_20261115_204125 only. Section 7.1 says failed or stopped attempts are recorded locally and never read by code. recover-glass (fix3) parsed this run's failed GLASS execution record, so the run does not comply literally with that rule. Recovery used the failed record only as a locator and a statement of scope: run id and step, code identity, execution status, notebook copy paths and hashes, gate checks, and inventory. Every value that became evidence was rebuilt from primary files or checked against them: the truncated copy was rebuilt from the committed notebook; both notebook copies were hashed and checked as one complete execution with no error and every legacy Stage 2 cell skipped; the model folders were compared byte for byte and classified against the passed preflight inventory; restoring only the recovery's files reproduced the preflight code identity; and the PR 38 acceptance and the Stage 2 pins were re-verified (A4.R 28/28). The failed record never became evidence. It stays Git-ignored and uncommitted, and it is named only by SHA-256. finalize and this acceptance hash it without reading it and require it to be unchanged. A4.3-A4.6 were recomputed from the artifacts. No other failed attempt was parsed. The contract has no exception clause for 7.1 and is not amended. I accept this as a recorded run-specific deviation under A4.7's explicit decision, following the recorded owner dispositions of D3 and section 7.4. Later runs must not read failed attempts.

7.2.statement: Section 7.2, run c4_20261115_204125 only. No record was replaced: each matches its sidecar, and later records name earlier ones by SHA-256. The run's code identity changed twice, each time through a registered step written once. Each step names its failed attempt by SHA-256 and records both code identities and every changed file: recover-glass (fix3, 7 files) and finalize-transition commit4a-t1 (fix4, 7 files, with my authorization recorded in finalize_transition.json). Every changed file is under upstream_regeneration/ or its tests, which no notebook imports, so no artifact was produced under changed code: the GLASS notebook ran under the preflight code and the black-box notebook under the recovered code. This acceptance re-derives both earlier identities from the tree and the recorded file hashes. It runs the run's own validation code, with only its two new files added. I approve the transition as recorded. The contract is not amended; any code change within a later run needs its own registered, owner-authorized step.
